text.en: Asha cut a stem and saw rings. "Plants have an inner structure like us," said her teacher.

Plant tissues are grouped into three tissue systems. The dermal or epidermal system forms the outer covering, the ground tissue system forms the bulk of the plant and the vascular tissue system, with xylem and phloem, conducts water and food. Monocot and dicot roots and stems differ in the arrangement of these tissues.
Plastids are cell structures, and the chloroplast, with chlorophyll, is where photosynthesis takes place. Photosynthesis uses light, carbon dioxide and water to make glucose and oxygen, and sunlight plays the key role. The light reaction happens in the grana and the dark reaction in the stroma of the chloroplast.
The plant also respires, taking in oxygen to release energy from food, and the chapter compares photosynthesis and respiration.

problem.en: Which tissue system carries water in a plant?

prompt.en: A friend says Photosynthesis happens in the mitochondria. How will you reply?

points.en: Three tissue systems: dermal, ground and vascular.
Xylem carries water, phloem carries food.
Chloroplast is the site of photosynthesis.
